We used to present, in this gathering, an explanation of the Book of God the Mighty, "falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it; it is a revelation from One Wise, Praiseworthy" [Fussilat 42], and which every Muslim must learn from its meanings what he needs for the matters of his religion and his worldly life. This is because God only sent down the Qur'an for recitation, reflection (tadabbur) and admonition (ittiʿaz). That is to say: the purpose of sending down the Qur'an is not merely that we worship God by reciting it, but that we worship Him by reciting it, understanding its meanings and acting upon it. The proof for this is the saying of God, blessed and exalted: "A Book We have sent down to you, blessed, that they may reflect upon its verses" [Sad 29]. He did not say: that they may recite it verbally. He said: "that they may reflect upon its verses and that those of understanding may be reminded" [Sad 29]. "They reflect upon them": they comprehend their meaning; "they are reminded by them": they act upon them.

We have now reached, in this initial tafsir from Surat al-Naba' to Surat al-Inshirah, the saying of the Exalted: "Did We not expand for you your breast? And We removed from you your burden, which had weighed upon your back, and We raised high for you your mention" [al-Sharh 1–4]. The raising of the Messenger's mention, peace and blessings be upon him, is something no one doubts, for his name is raised at every prayer in the highest of places. And how is that? In the adhan: "I bear witness that there is no god but God, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God."

Second: His mention is raised in every prayer as an obligation in the tashahhud, for the tashahhud is obligatory, and in it: "I bear witness that there is no god but God, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger."

Third: His mention is raised in every act of worship. Every act of worship includes the mention of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. How so? Because every act of worship must have two fundamental conditions: sincerity to God, and following the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. It is well known that one who follows the Messenger will, during worship, bring to mind that he is following the Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, and this is part of raising his mention.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 94, verses 5–6:

﴿So indeed, with hardship comes ease (5). Indeed, with hardship comes ease (6).﴾ [al-Sharh: 5, 6] This is good news from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to the Messenger (ﷺ) and to the entire Ummah. We ask: did hardship befall the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him)? And where was he in it?

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. When he was in Makkah, he was constricted in Makkah, and in Ta'if, and likewise also in Madinah, from the hypocrites.

So Allah says: ﴿So indeed, with hardship comes ease﴾, meaning: just as We expanded your breast, removed from you your burden, and raised high your remembrance, and these are great blessings, so too this hardship that befalls you must have ease.

﴿So indeed, with hardship comes ease (5). Indeed, with hardship comes ease﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said about this verse: "One hardship will never overcome two eases."[[Narrated by al-Hakim (3994) from al-Hasan, from the Prophet (ﷺ), as a mursal report; it is also reported as a saying of 'Umar, 'Ali and Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with them). al-Sakhawi said in al-Maqasid al-Hasanah (p. 339): "On this topic there is a report from Ibn 'Abbas as his own statement; al-Farra' related it from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from him."]] So what is the explanation of his statement, may Allah be pleased with him, given that "hardship" is mentioned twice and "ease" is mentioned twice?

The scholars of rhetoric said: The explanation of his statement is that "hardship" is mentioned only once. In ﴿So indeed, with hardship comes ease (5). Indeed, with hardship comes ease﴾, the first "hardship" is repeated in the second with the definite article (al), so the (al) here is the definite of prior mention (al-'ahd al-dhikri). As for "ease" (yusr), it does not come definite but indefinite. The rule is that when a noun is repeated twice in indefinite form, the second is different from the first, except in rare cases; and conversely, when a noun is repeated twice in definite form, the second is the same as the first, except in rare cases.

Pay attention to this rule. The rule now: when a noun is repeated twice in definite form, the second is the first, except in rare cases; and when a noun is repeated twice in indefinite form, the second is other than the first, because the second is indefinite and so is other than the first.

Therefore, in the two noble verses there are two eases and one hardship, because "hardship" is repeated twice in definite form.

﴿So indeed, with hardship comes ease﴾: this statement is from whom? From Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and His report is the most complete of reports in truthfulness, and His promise is not broken. So whenever a matter becomes hard for you, my brother, then await ease.

As for legislated matters, it is clear. "Pray standing; if you cannot, then sitting; if you cannot, then lying on your side."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (1117) from the hadith of 'Imran ibn Husayn (may Allah be pleased with him).]] This is ease: if standing is hard for you, sit; if sitting is hard for you, pray while lying on your side.

In fasting: if you are able while resident, then fast; if you are not able, then break your fast; if you are traveling, then break your fast.

In Hajj: if you are able to reach it, then perform Hajj; if you are not able, then there is no Hajj upon you. Rather, if you have begun Hajj and a circumstance arises that prevents you from completing it, then exit the state of ihram, cancel the Hajj, and offer a sacrifice; because of the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah. But if you are prevented, then [send] what is easy of sacrifice﴾ [al-Baqarah: 196].

So every hardship that occurs for a person in worship finds facilitation and ease.

Likewise in qada' and qadar: that is, Allah's decree upon a person of calamities, constriction of livelihood, constriction of the breast, and other things. Let him not despair: ﴿So indeed, with hardship comes ease﴾. Ease may be something apparent and sensory, such as a person being poor and matters constricting for him, so Allah makes wealth easy for him. This is sensory ease. Is this not so?

A person who is sick, who suffers, for whom illness is hard, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, cures him: this too is sensory ease.

There is also moral ease, which is Allah's help to the person in patience. This is ease: when Allah helps you to be patient, the difficult becomes easy for you. This matter, which if it descended upon the mountains would crush them, becomes a simple matter through the patience with which Allah has helped you. Do not think that ease means that something opens up once; no, ease is that distress is relieved and removed, and this is sensory ease; and that Allah helps the person to be patient until this severe, difficult matter becomes easy for him. We say this because we are confident in Allah's promise: ﴿So indeed, with hardship comes ease (5). Indeed, with hardship comes ease﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 94, verse 7:

﴿So when you are free, then strive hard (7). And to your Lord direct your longing﴾ [al-Sharh: 7, 8]. The meaning is that this verse means: when you have finished your works, then strive (infsab) for another work; that is, exert yourself for another work. Do not let the world be wasted on you. For this reason, the life of the sensible person is a life of earnestness: whenever he finishes one task, he starts on another, with no wasting of time. Time does not show mercy, as they say. Time moves on; it escapes a person in his waking and his sleeping, in his busyness and his leisure. It flows. Can anyone hold back time? No, it is not possible. Even if all creatures gathered to stop the sun so that the day would lengthen, they would not be able to do it. Time cannot be held by anyone.

So make your life one of earnestness (jidd). When you finish a work, strive in another work. When you finish with the affairs of this world, turn to the affairs of the Hereafter; when you finish with the affairs of the Hereafter, busy yourself with the affairs of this world. ﴿So when the prayer is concluded﴾ on Friday. The Friday prayer is surrounded by two worldly acts: ﴿O you who believe, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trade. That is better for you, if you only knew (9). And when the prayer is concluded, disperse within the land and seek of the bounty of Allah﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 9, 10]. That is, while you are occupied with your worldly affairs. "Hasten" (fas'aw), "trade" (bay'), "buy and sell": when we finish one occupation, we occupy ourselves with another; when we finish it, we occupy ourselves with another. Thus the person ought always to be in earnestness.

If someone says: if I used earnestness throughout my whole life, I would become exhausted and weary.

We say: your rest, to revitalize yourself and renew your energy, is considered what? It is considered work and action. That is, it is not necessary that work be movement; rather, your leisure in order to become energized for the next task is considered work. The important thing is that you make your whole life earnestness, work.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 94, verse 8:

﴿So when you are free, then strive hard (7), and to your Lord turn with desire﴾. That is: when you have done the tasks you were free from and worked hard at the others, then turn with desire to Allah, mighty and majestic, for what? Turn to Allah for the attainment of reward, for the attainment of recompense, for help. Be with Allah, mighty and majestic, before the deed and after the deed. Before the deed, be with Allah, seeking His help, mighty and majestic; and after it, hope from Him for reward; ﴿and to your Lord turn with desire﴾.

Regarding His words ﴿to your Lord turn with desire﴾, there is a rhetorical benefit about which I will ask you: ﴿to your Lord﴾ is connected to what? Grammatically, it is connected to ﴿turn with desire﴾ (irghab), placed before it, and fronting the object (taqdim al-ma'mul) gives exclusivity (al-hasr); meaning: to Allah and not to other than Him. So turn with desire in all your affairs, and be assured that whenever you attach your desire to Allah, mighty and majestic, He will certainly make your affairs easy for you. Many people lack this state; that is, they lack constantly being those who turn with desire to Allah, so you find that much of their work is disordered, because there was no connection between them and Allah, exalted is He, in their works.

We ask Allah, glorified and exalted, to make us and you among those who comply with His commands and affirm His reports, indeed He is capable of all things.
